versions.lyricRevisionNote: Revision v0.8: a native-speaker review of syntax applied over the rhymed text, and one rhyme rolled back. Accepted: st.4 'suyetnaya' -> 'brennaya' (yd'le as transitory, on the reviewer's reading of the 2005 notes - recorded as a lead, not verified); st.6 plural 'v grekhakh ... Tvorya ikh' (de snooden sonden is plural); st.6 'nachnite zhizn dobrodetelnuyu' for het deugdsaam leven; st.7 'V Nyom odnom' for alleen, dash removed; st.9 'lyubov lyudskaya, lyudskiye nravy' (seden plural) and 'ten yeyo' restoring the 'van'; st.10 'Poyte vovek' (Singt is plural). Rejected: no negation is restored in st.8 (the print reads 'nog' with an affirmative verb); 'zhizn dobrodeteli' is a correct rendering of 'der deugden leven' genitive plural, only the closing line was wrong; the tripled word stays an infinitive because the Dutch is an infinitive. Rhyme rolled back in st.2: the close returns to 'Sertsu tsenu dayot vyshe vsekh' because the rhyme had been bought with a word not in the line. Tags shortened to three structural marks. Stress marks: four. Russian adaptation; owner revision is the gate. Revision v0.9: stanza 1, owner's decision - the fourth 'prakh' removed. Line 9 now reads 'Sertsa tvoyego ne stoit', the print's shape (op aard three times, then a different word, niet waard). Stanza 1 leaves the full-rhyme column, as stanza 2 did in v0.8 and for the same reason; tally now three met, four half, three not met. Close 8 syllables, metre row 6-6-6-8 | 5 | 9 | 8. No other line, mark or tag changed; both lyric files 90 lines and identical apart from tags, echo and the four marks. Revision v0.10: stanza 3, line 2 — «После земных невзгод» replaced by «Та, что за смертью придёт», because the Dutch line is 'Na dit leven crijgelijck' and the 2005 apparatus glosses it as the life to be obtained after this life; the reading was verified in the 1676 print, the 1727 edition and the 2005 edition (COLLATION_DUTCH-005_THREE_WAY.md). Chosen from three counted options (DUTCH-005_STANZA_3_2_OPTIONS.md); seven syllables, rhyme with line 4 preserved. No other line changed.

versions.lyricRevisionNote: v0.5 (changelog): the owner caught a broken syntax in v0.4 — «блаженного, Иисус Христос» is a genitive followed by a nominative in the same list, which Russian cannot read. The address is now at the head of line 1 («Иисус Христос, свет отрадный святой славы»), with the same words and the same cases; only the name moved. Two consequences, both recorded as losses: the Greek word order of lines 1–2 is not kept, and the suspended reference of the three genitive adjectives is gone — they now read as attributes of the Father, the case-faithful solution. «Иисуса Христа» was rejected with three reasons (it would join the genitive chain and make Christ a second name for the Father; the Greek has a vocative, not a genitive, there). The refrain is unchanged; the reprise moved from line 1 to line 6, because after the reorder line 1 ends on the genitive «славы» and would cut the hymn mid-phrase. Syllables by machine: 13, 17, 14, 16, 20, 15. Five stress marks — the mark on «Иису́с» was wrongly dropped in v0.4 and is restored. v0.4 (changelog): on 2026-10-26 the owner directed a level, non-Church-Slavonic register («без православной стилистики, сделай ровнее»), so the two vocatives were replaced by the nominative: line 2 «Иисус Христос» (was «Иисусе Христе»), line 6 «Сын Божий» (was «Сыне Божий»). The Greek vocative is therefore not rendered as a case — a named loss, not a re-wording of the same thing. Machine-counted syllables: 14, 16, 14, 16, 20, 15; four stress marks, the one on the name no longer needed. The other four lines are unchanged, and the earlier changelog entries below still stand as history. v0.2 (changelog): the owner directed a closer, more literal translation on 2026-10-26 — if the source has rhyme, keep it; if not, do not add it; translate from the Greek rather than from the Church Slavonic. v0.3 (changelog): the owner chose the reading and the title on 2026-10-26 — «Давай как в греческом и Свет Отрадный». ἱλαρόν is «отрадный» (the owner's decision; the dictionary-literal «радостный» was tried in v0.2 and is named in the dossier, not hidden), the title «Свет Отрадный» is approved, and the vocatives plus the suspended reference of the three genitive adjectives are confirmed as in the Greek. The six Greek lines map one content word per Russian word and keep the Greek order; exactly one auxiliary is added («быть» in line 5, without which Russian cannot render the passive infinitive), only the articles are dropped, and one pair of words is reordered in line 3 («закату солнца» for «солнца закату»). Rhyme and metre: checked, not assumed — the six Greek line-endings (Πατρός, Χριστέ, ἑσπερινόν, Θεόν, αἰσίαις, δοξάζει) do not rhyme and the syllable counts are 15·15·18·16·16·18, so nothing was preserved and nothing added. No refrain, no repeated line, no added line. The suspended reference of the three genitive adjectives is preserved. Russian syllables counted by machine: 14, 17, 14, 16, 20, 16. Five stress marks in the stage text. A working draft, not an owner-approved text. Arrangement added on 2026-10-26 at the owner's direction; the six-line translation was not altered — every repeated line is an exact repetition of a line already in it.

interpretationNotes: The three genitive adjectives now read as attributes of the Father: the Greek ambiguity cannot survive a nominative address. Resolved in favour of the case, not of the majority translation; variant В resolves it the other way and is documented.

The nominative «Иисус Христос» / «Сын Божий» is an address by position and context, not by form: Russian lost the vocative, and the Church Slavonic -е forms would have raised the register above the Greek, which uses the vocative neutrally. The owner chose register over case.
